findings.title: Exception Type Change
findings.body: This only matters for unusual errno values. `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` are handled, and `EACCES`/`EPERM` still map to `UnauthorizedAccessException`. Any other `opendir`/`readdir` failure, such as `EIO`, `EMFILE` or `ENFILE` (fd exhaustion is plausible in a process that is itself being monitored for handle counts), now throws `Win32Exception`. The old `Directory.GetFiles` path threw an `IOException`-derived exception for these errors. `Win32Exception` is not an `IOException`, so callers that read `HandleCount` and catch `IOException` would see a different exception. Mapping the fallback through `Interop.GetExceptionForIoErrno(error, path)` would preserve the previous exception types.

Exception Type Change
This only matters for unusual errno values. `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` are handled, and `EACCES`/`EPERM` still map to `UnauthorizedAccessException`. Any other `opendir`/`readdir` failure, such as `EIO`, `EMFILE` or `ENFILE` (fd exhaustion is plausible in a process that is itself being monitored for handle counts), now throws `Win32Exception`. The old `Directory.GetFiles` path threw an `IOException`-derived exception for these errors. `Win32Exception` is not an `IOException`, so callers that read `HandleCount` and catch `IOException` would see a different exception. Mapping the fallback through `Interop.GetExceptionForIoErrno(error, path)` would preserve the previous exception types.
